title: Darwin: Evolution Revolution
description: One voyage, one book—five steps from a Royal Navy ship to the theory that changed biology.

questions.question: What is the title of Darwin's groundbreaking 1859 book that introduced the theory of evolution?
acceptedAnswers: on the origin of species by means of natural selection
questions.hint: It's about the 'origin' of all living things and their different types
questions.explanation: Irony: the word "evolution" never appears in the first edition—its very last word is "evolved." Booksellers ordered more copies than the 1,250 printed.

questions.question: Darwin's Origin draws on years aboard what Royal Navy survey ship?
questions.hint: Named after a type of hunting dog, this royal navy ship sailed around the world
questions.explanation: Captain Robert FitzRoy, a believer in reading faces, nearly rejected Darwin over the shape of his nose, Darwin later wrote. The voyage ran almost five years; he was seasick throughout.

questions.question: Aboard the Beagle, Darwin collected finches from what Pacific archipelago?
questions.hint: These volcanic islands are off the coast of Ecuador, famous for unique species
questions.explanation: The Beagle stayed just five weeks. The vice-governor said he could tell a tortoise's home island by its shell—Darwin missed the hint, and the crew ate their tortoises.

questions.question: Back in London, ornithologist John Gould showed those Galápagos birds were separate species—evidence that led Darwin toward what mechanism?
questions.hint: Nature 'selects' the best traits, or only the 'fittest' survive
questions.explanation: Myth: the finches gave Darwin his eureka on the islands. Actually, he didn't even label them by island; Gould's 1837 analysis (and the islands' mockingbirds) mattered more, and natural selection took shape in 1838.

questions.question: Long before natural selection, Darwin went to Cambridge to train as a country parson—studying what?
questions.hint: He originally studied to become a clergyman and understand God's word
questions.explanation: Strictly, it was an ordinary Cambridge BA, the usual route to ordination. The twist: the would-be parson who rattled the Church was buried in Westminster Abbey, near Isaac Newton.

imageHint: Finches, fossils, and the puzzle of adaptation

deeperMode.title: Darwin's Tormented Genius
deeperMode.description: Personal struggle behind a world-changing theory

questions.question: Darwin paced a gravel path in his garden while pondering evolution. What did he call it?
questions.hint: He would drop pebbles to count his laps while deep in thought about natural selection

questions.question: What chronic health problem plagued Darwin for most of his adult life, possibly worsened by stress over his revolutionary theory?
questions.hint: Modern doctors think it was stress-related, causing stomach problems and exhaustion
